scope: Ordinary torch.compile on four trained checkpoints from test/fixtures/main_legacy. These CPU checks use one timed repetition to verify behavior and gradients. Phase 0 has its own snapshot matrix.
method: Each side ran on the same CPU allocation, in a separate process, using one model/precision-specific compilation cache. The training step differentiates sum(E squared) + sum(Fa squared) with respect to the model weights. Cross-source gradients were compared under their original trained parameter names. The molecular cases reused the per-side caches generated in calibration. The periodic and large cases started with empty caches.
training_dispatch: The MACE FF04 checkpoint builds scripted e3nn force kernels. Its ordinary compiled training call dispatches to native forces. SchNet, PhysNet and SpookyNet select the compiled coordinate VJP. Graph counters and returned autograd functions describe the observations in each process.

single_structure_scatter_followup.reason: In PyTorch 2.13.0+cu126, CPU Inductor CppVecKernel.store asserted index.is_vec while generating the original [1, 3] atomic-add destination in trained PhysNet force fitting. The first system in each precision was the original standalone failing input: periodic 256 for float64 and nonperiodic 2000 for float32. The correction preserves a spare destination during lowering.
single_structure_scatter_followup.baseline_order_observation: In the float64 follow-up, the original main failed on periodic 256 first. The later 32x20 inference reported donated buffers, whereas the independent process starting with 32x20 validated that inference. Each row records its ordered systems and error separately.
